help: Maximum length of the final summary in characters (100 to 20000). Longer replies are cut at a word or a whole bullet and flagged truncated.
bullets: a list of short points. paragraph: one block of text.
same: the language of the text. en: English. fr: French.
OpenAI-compatible API root; the block calls <api_base_url>/chat/completions or /responses. Loopback servers (Ollama, LM Studio, vLLM) work as is; other hosts need allow_remote.
Model name sent to the endpoint. Prefer a model that follows JSON instructions reliably.
Optional wallet reference for a Bearer API key, e.g. secret://workspace/llm_key. Never paste the key itself.
chat_completions: POST /chat/completions, supported by most servers. responses: POST /responses (OpenAI Responses API).
Ask the endpoint for JSON that follows a JSON schema (response_format json_schema). Turn off if the server rejects it; the reply is validated either way.
Sampling temperature from 0 to 2. 0 gives the most repeatable answers. Leave empty to let the server decide (some reasoning models refuse this parameter).
Maximum tokens of one reply (16 to 65536), or 0 to not send a limit. A reply cut by this limit counts as invalid.
Total time allowed for one message, every request and the retry included (1 to 600 seconds).

placeholder: Messages come from the support inbox of a bicycle shop.
help: Optional context added to the model instructions, e.g. who writes the texts. At most 4000 characters.
Empty: analyze the whole message. Otherwise a path in a JSON message, e.g. body.message or items[0].text; it must lead to a text.
Longest text accepted, in characters (default 100000). A longer text is refused on error.
summarize: texts longer than this are summarized in parts of about this many characters, then combined.
summarize: maximum number of parts of one text (1 to 64).
Allow a non-loopback endpoint (LAN or Internet). Off by default; link-local and metadata addresses stay blocked.
Allow plain HTTP to a non-loopback host. An API key is never sent this way.
Optional absolute path of a PEM CA file for an HTTPS endpoint with a private certificate authority.
Largest endpoint response accepted, in bytes.
